91.title: Mother and Son
91.scene: Mercedes and Albert renounce the Morcerf name and fortune

words.d: formally giving up a claim - name, title and money together
to refuse to accept or be associated with
of money: contaminated by the crime that produced it
the poverty they deliberately choose
Mercedes Herrera, reclaimed
where she will return, the circle closing
Albert's decision: the army in Africa, under another name
to atone for another's sin by one's own suffering
utterly without means
what they keep; Dumas is careful to let them keep it
the end of the Morcerf thread
what he cannot survive, though he survived the treason
being cut by everyone one knows
his last attempt: he goes to the Count for an answer
'Edmond Dantes!' - the name that kills him
the sound of the shot heard from the carriage
the emptied house
inescapable retribution
brought to completion - the first of the four falls
without pity; and note the Count's first flicker of doubt

93.title: Valentine
93.scene: Valentine is poisoned and the Count intervenes

words.d: the counter-poison the Count has been administering in secret
a preventive treatment given before harm
small increasing quantities building tolerance
a return of illness after apparent recovery
feverish confusion of mind
the night watch kept over the sick
the Count stepping inside his own machine to stop it
the flaw in his theory of providence
harm falling on those the plan never targeted
a sharp prick of conscience

94.title: Maximilian's Avowal
94.scene: Maximilian declares his love for Valentine

words.d: an open declaration of something previously hidden
the formal statement of love and intent to marry
a formal courtship pressed to a father
a blunt refusal
what Villefort considers a soldier's son marrying his daughter
stubborn refusal to yield
the state Maximilian is driven to
to entrust a secret - to the Count, who already knows
the Count's protection, silently extended over this pair
burning intensity of feeling

95.title: Father and Daughter
95.scene: Danglars and Eugenie over the marriage he has arranged

words.d: a match settled by parents for money and rank
the sum that makes Eugenie a commodity
what Eugenie wants instead - and names explicitly
her chosen identity: a musician, self-supporting
hard refusal to be moved
how both father and daughter openly describe the marriage
legally required, and extracted under pressure
Eugenie's startling frankness about wanting no husband
the truth behind Danglars' haste to sell her
the force behind a formally free choice

96.title: The Contract
96.scene: The signing is interrupted by the gendarmes

words.d: the notarised settlement signed before the wedding
the official drawing and reading the contract aloud
those who sign; the assembled society of the novel
the property settled on the couple
the gendarmes at the door - a deliberate echo of chapter 5
the arrest order for Andrea Cavalcanti
the charge read out in the drawing room
the guests', exactly as at the betrothal feast in Marseille
Andrea's escape through the dressing-room window
the frozen scene; Dumas stages it as theatre
social, instant, and total

97.title: The Departure for Belgium
97.scene: Eugenie and Louise cut their hair and take the road

words.d: the two women leaving together, on their own terms
the travel document, obtained under a false name
Eugenie's man's clothing and cropped hair
the hired carriage for the flight
the destination; Belgium as the standard bolt-hole of the ruined
self-rule; the thing Eugenie has wanted from the start
the music school career she intends
free of paternal control
how Paris will describe it; Dumas lets her not care
firmly determined

98.title: The Bell and Bottle Tavern
98.scene: Andrea is run to ground at Compiegne

words.d: the roadside stop where he is taken
town north of Paris on the Belgian road
one fleeing arrest
the state police force pursuing him
the circulated physical account of a wanted man
to arrest
his hiding place; the ignominy is the point
the restraints he wore before, and wears again
showy defiance covering fear
being held by the law

99.title: The Law
99.scene: The machinery of justice takes hold of Benedetto

words.d: the impersonal machine Villefort serves and will be crushed by
the Paris prison where Benedetto is held
the judge who interrogates before trial
being formally sent for trial
one carrying the death penalty
the lawyer assigned to a defendant
detention while awaiting trial
an earlier case guiding a decision
the forms of law - which Villefort once bent for himself
the prosecutor preparing the case against his own son

100.title: The Apparition
100.scene: Valentine, half-drugged, sees a figure in her room

words.d: the Count, appearing as if supernatural
the hidden entry from the neighbouring house
drowsy, half-asleep
a sleep-inducing drug
the Count swapping the poisoned draught
he has been watching the room for weeks
the role he assumes, half-ironically
the death-like trance he is preparing for her
ready to believe; Valentine half-thinks she is dreaming
the false death being set up

101.title: Locusta
101.scene: Madame de Villefort at her work

words.d: professional poisoner of Nero's Rome - the chapter's title and verdict
the small bottle of poison
the pharmacist; the source of the drugs
the written order for a medicine - and the cover
the careful calibration of a killing
who benefits: Edouard, her son, inherits at every death
the motive; Dumas insists the murders are acts of mother-love
systematic, unhurried - the horror of it
the fixed idea that has consumed her
the word the novel finally reaches for
the drugged trance mistaken for death
stiffness of the body taken as proof
absent to every test the doctor applies
to prepare a body for burial
those who sit with the dead through the night
to declare death officially
Noirtier's, expressed entirely through the eyes
d'Avrigny and Noirtier now both know who
the Count's, kept even from Maximilian - and this costs him
a deep trance-like unconsciousness

103.title: Maximilian
103.scene: Maximilian's grief; the Count asks him to wait a month

words.d: loss by death
laid low, overwhelmed by grief
he resolves on suicide, as his father once did
the one month the Count asks him to grant life
the promise extracted: wait, and then judge
the Count names himself as the Morrel family's benefactor
the obligation that binds Maximilian to obey
comfort in sorrow
endurance under suffering
the fifth of September again; Dumas loves a date

104.title: Danglars' Signature
104.scene: The Count draws down the banker's last reserves

words.d: the signed order to pay - five of them, a million each
to take money out against a credit
the cash a bank holds against demands
creditors demanding payment at once
the charity money Danglars takes to cover the gap
theft of money placed in one's trust
to flee with money one has stolen
the five millions he carries into Italy
the third house to fall
the winding-up that follows his flight

105.title: The Cemetery of Pere-Lachaise
105.scene: Valentine's funeral; the Count and Maximilian at the tomb

words.d: the great Paris cemetery
a grand tomb building
a speech in praise of the dead
the funeral procession
the graveyard tree, emblem of mourning
the inscription on a tomb
beyond comfort
the funeral rites
violation of something sacred - the thought of the empty coffin
Maximilian's, which the Count must break

106.title: Dividing the Proceeds
106.scene: Debray and Madame Danglars settle accounts and part

words.d: the profits of their years of insider speculation
the term Debray uses for the affair - and he means it
the itemised statement he presents her
a half share
to wind up a partnership
to square the books before separating
the exact temperature of the scene
the silence both now need from the other
morally grubby, mean about money
hers, complete and final

107.title: The Lions' Den
107.scene: Benedetto in prison; Bertuccio visits him

words.d: prison slang for the yard holding the worst offenders
the private slang of thieves and convicts
a jailer
where those facing death are held
the prison's own economy of betrayal
the fact Benedetto is about to weaponise
Bertuccio tells him whose son he is
the hold this gives him over the prosecutor
showing no repentance
Benedetto's defining register

108.title: The Judge
108.scene: Villefort confronts his wife and gives her an ultimatum

words.d: a final demand with a stated consequence
the case he has silently built against his own wife
the public execution he offers her as the alternative
the poison he orders her to take
encouraging a crime - what his ultimatum amounts to
the judge dispensing private death to avoid public shame
his manner, learned in twenty years of prosecuting
one condemned and beyond redemption
the word he uses for what he is doing; judge it yourself
the child neither parent is thinking about; remember him

109.title: The Assizes
109.scene: The court assembles for Benedetto's trial

words.d: the criminal court sitting for the gravest charges
where the accused stands
the judges
the twelve who decide the facts
the public seats - packed, for this one
the officer who keeps order in court
to call a prisoner forward and put the charge to them
to answer the charge guilty or not guilty
a trial that becomes a public sensation
the court's formal dignity, about to be destroyed

110.title: The Indictment
110.scene: Benedetto names his father in open court

words.d: the formal reading of the charges
conducted by Villefort himself
the question the accused turns into a weapon
the legal fact of descent from a particular parent
killing a parent - the charge hanging over the courtroom
the uproar in the gallery
to suspend the court's sitting
Villefort's, made standing in his own court
to give up an office - he resigns on the spot
total public disgrace
the prosecutor destroyed by the forms he perfected

111.title: Expiation
111.scene: Villefort comes home to find his wife and son dead

words.d: atonement through suffering - the novel's key term
deserved punishment
the child his mother takes with her; the Count's unbearable miscalculation
the word that breaks the Count's whole philosophy
to try to revive - the Count's frantic, failed attempt
madness; Villefort's mind gives way
the loss of reason he ends in
unmixed, and Dumas does not soften it
the Count's sin: believing he was Providence
what the Count must now make, and the rest of the book is about
the madman's last occupation in the garden

112.title: The Departure
112.scene: The Count settles his affairs and leaves Paris

words.d: the withdrawal from the city he came to destroy
to convert property into money and close accounts
arrangements made for others' futures
where Albert goes as a private soldier
an officer's rank - which Albert refuses to buy
the Count's habit; here, the money left for Mercedes
a farewell
doubt about what one has done
the accounting now being made, by him, of himself
new to him since Edouard; watch it grow

113.title: The Past
113.scene: Marseille again: the Catalans, the old house, Mercedes

words.d: a return journey to a place of meaning
his father's house, bought and preserved
a kept object charged with memory - the purse, the room
recollection of the past
Mercedes' now: she refuses everything but a little
acceptance without bitterness - her final state
his, for the first time given full voice
impossible to undo
of a kind: not reunion, but peace
the span the two of them now measure out loud

114.title: Peppino
114.scene: Danglars arrives in Rome and is taken

words.d: the bandit whose life the Count bought in chapter 35 - now collecting
where the last account is settled
the five millions Danglars is carrying
Thomson and French, who cash it - and report it
the carriage that turns off the road
seizure by force
the underground prison of Vampa's band
the bandit; here, an instrument of justice
he has been watched since he crossed the border
the machinery closing on the last of the four

115.title: Luigi Vampa's Bill of Fare
115.scene: Danglars is starved and charged a fortune for each meal

words.d: a menu - the chapter's grim joke
charging outrageously - a hundred thousand francs a fowl
the starvation deliberately inflicted
to give in to terms
the vice being surgically operated on
the man who starved Dantes' father is starved for money
the measured allowance of food
the stripping away of everything but appetite
brought low - the word Dumas keeps using
his, extracted franc by franc

116.title: The Pardon
116.scene: The Count reveals himself and lets Danglars go, white-haired

words.d: the release granted at the moment it is no longer wanted
genuine sorrow for wrongdoing - Danglars reaches it under starvation
'I am Edmond Dantes' - for the last time
mercy from one with the power to destroy
the mark the ordeal leaves on him
the five millions restored, less what was owed the hospitals
the Count's admission: he is a man, not Providence
the lesson Edouard's death taught him
the release from guilt he grants and seeks
the verb the whole revenge has been building toward

117.title: The Fifth of October
117.scene: Monte Cristo: Maximilian, Valentine, and the last words

words.d: the date of the month's expiry - and of the reunion
the island cave where the novel ends as it turned
Valentine given back, alive
the drug Maximilian believes will kill him; it does not
the book's governing figure, completed
the island and the fortune, left to the young pair
the Count gives up the treasure and the name together
who refuses to be freed, and is not left behind
'attendre et esperer' - the novel's last and most quoted words
deep happiness - the state the last page finally permits
the Count's parting blessing on the living
